title: Remove Duplicate Letters
statement: Remove repeated letters so each distinct character appears once and the result is the smallest lexicographic string possible.
explanation: Keep a stack of chosen characters. Before adding a character, remove larger stack-top characters that occur again later.

title: Maximum Product of Word Lengths
statement: Find the maximum product of lengths of two words that share no letters.
explanation: Encode each word's letters as bits and compare masks with bitwise AND.

title: Bulb Switcher
statement: There are n bulbs toggled on successive rounds by multiples of each round number. Return how many bulbs remain on.
explanation: Only positions with an odd number of divisors remain on; exactly perfect squares have an odd divisor count.

title: Coin Change
statement: Return the fewest coins needed to make amount using unlimited coins of the supplied denominations, or -1 if impossible.
explanation: For every amount, try each coin and extend the best solution for the remaining amount.

title: Power of Three
statement: Determine whether an integer n is a power of three.
explanation: Within positive 32-bit integers, the largest power of three is divisible by every smaller power of three and by no non-power.

title: Odd Even Linked List
statement: Group nodes at odd positions followed by nodes at even positions, preserving relative order within each group.
explanation: Link odd-position nodes together and even-position nodes together, then append the even chain after the odd chain.

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
statement: Return the length of the longest path in a matrix that moves orthogonally and strictly increases at every step.
explanation: Memoize the longest increasing path starting at each cell; only move to strictly larger neighbors.

title: Verify Preorder Serialization of a Binary Tree
statement: Determine whether a comma-separated preorder serialization with # for null children describes a valid binary tree.
explanation: Start with one available child slot; each node consumes a slot and each non-null node creates two new slots.

title: Reconstruct Itinerary
statement: Use every flight ticket exactly once to reconstruct an itinerary starting at JFK, choosing the lexicographically smallest valid itinerary.
explanation: Sort each airport's destinations in reverse lexical order and perform DFS while consuming edges, then reverse the postorder route.

title: Increasing Triplet Subsequence
statement: Return whether an array contains indices i<j<k with nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k].
explanation: Track the smallest first and second values seen; a value larger than both completes a triplet.
